81894.body:
Daily Crypto Digest

Автор: Oleh Bezuhlyi


Автор: Oleh Bezuhlyi

https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/daily-crypto-digest-november-3-oleh-bezuhlyi-dbumf?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3Bg0JR6DBRS6ObjgV3MXObog%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=0xIaAW-70caYw1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mw0q94lx~jf-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mw0q94lx-jf
  
🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin hovers near $77K as US midterm voting, ETF outflows and Binance-hack fallout keep traders defensive. Early recovery signals are emerging, but sentiment remains firmly in fear territory. 📉 Bitcoin Steadies Near $76,900 as ETF Outflows and Midterms Weigh Bitcoin dipped to about $76,300 during the European morning before stabilizing near $76,900. US spot bitcoin ETFs shed $399 million on Monday — a second straight day of outflows — with BlackRock's IBIT losing $405 million, its biggest daily exit since June. Options traders are bracing for volatility around today's US midterm vote, pushing near-dated implied volatility to roughly 51%. Read full story 🏦 Binance Net Outflows Hit $5.3B as Hourly Deposits Turn Positive Users pulled $10.97 billion from Binance in the 46 hours after its record $6.4 billion hack, leaving net outflows of $5.28 billion, according to on-chain data shared by CEO Richard Teng. Withdrawal pressure peaked on Nov. 1, but by early Nov. 3 hourly deposits exceeded withdrawals by about $10 million — a shift Teng cites as a sign of stabilization. More details 🇰🇵 North Korea Denies Role in $6.4B Binance Hack Kim Yo Jong, sister of leader Kim Jong Un, dismissed the FBI's attribution of the theft to the TraderTraitor group as a political provocation in a statement carried by state agency KCNA. Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic countered that on-chain evidence backs the FBI and said $2.85 billion of the stolen funds has already been frozen or seized. Read more ⚖️ SEC Clarifies When DAO Governance Signals Central Control The SEC's Division of Corporation Finance added three new answers to its crypto-asset FAQ, stating that unrelated token holders don't become a controlling group simply by voting — while coordinated blocs or concentrated delegated power may. The guidance also separates a functioning network from a truly decentralized one; it is a staff view with no legal force. See details 💰 Tether Says It Holds ~150,000 BTC Worth $11.5B Speaking at the Plan ₿ Forum in Lugano, CEO Paolo Ardoino said Tether holds roughly 150,000 bitcoin — about 50,000 more than its BDO-attested Q3 reserve report implies. He didn't say where the extra coins sit or when they were acquired; holdings outside USDT reserves, such as Tether's investments, wouldn't appear in that report. Read full story 🇧🇷 Mercado Bitcoin Will Cover Al

81883.subject: If Binance Isn’t Safe, What Is?
81883.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

It's been a while since I've done market talk, but this feels like a week worth discussing. Bitcoin closed its fourth consecutive week in the red, and yesterday's selloff suggests a fifth may be coming. The weakness hasn't been confined to crypto. Gold touched its lowest level in a year on Friday, and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq sold off again yesterday ahead of today's midterms; Polymarket gives Democrats a 76.5% chance of controlling the Senate. It's fair to say October was a good month to hold cash.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/797f4e9b-67c9-475c-9c8d-3439447679d6/image.png?t=1793716335)
Caption: 

I don't know whether this is a bull market correction or whether the rally has run its course. But looking beyond prices, what concerns me most about crypto right now is security. Last Thursday, Nick Carpinito's [newsletter](https://blockworks.com/newsletter/0xresearch/issue/post_f505e795-45bd-4ae9-823a-28f0f4c4e0c6) covered the rise in crypto exploits: more than 300 this year, up 111% YoY. Talk about timing, as later that same day Binance suffered the largest crypto theft ever, about $6.3B, roughly four times Bybit's $1.5B in 2025. Yesterday, Brazilian exchange Mercado Bitcoin suspended deposits and withdrawals after about $40M in unauthorized transfers.

The silver lining is that both exchanges say customers won't bear the losses. Binance has already resumed withdrawals, with about $3.0B in net outflows over the past 24 hours and $15.4B over the past seven days, which includes the hack itself. Notably, Binance still holds about $125B in assets and has the balance sheet to absorb outflows of this size, which is encouraging, but I think there's a deeper confidence problem at play. If even Binance, the largest exchange in the industry, can suffer a breach of this scale, it's hard to imagine someone who doesn't spend their time in crypto feeling comfortable allocating to it.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b974053b-4a9e-4034-8133-8126e078019d/image.png?t=1793716335)
Caption: 

After this year's self-custody incidents, I would have told a friend outside crypto to just keep their funds on a large exchange. A [Coldcard firmware flaw](https://www.trmlabs.com/resources/blog/the-largest-hardware-wallet-exploit-of-2026-inside-the-usd-116-million-coldcard-hack) let attackers drain about $116M in BTC in July, and last month [tampered Ledger devices](https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-ledger-supply-chain-attack-october-2026) sold through a reseller were linked to roughly $93M in losses. After last week's events, it seems that advic
